cmd: pnpm run check-types && pnpm run test:unit

testChange.reason: Two assertions in the shared harness had to move because this task removes the mechanism they pinned: makeDeps gains a stubbed `snapshot` (the in-process engine no longer copies, so stub deps that never touch a real file need it), and the engine-selection test now asserts deps.snapshot was called and deps.copy was not, where it previously asserted the live db was copied to the temp path. Nothing weakened — the copy assertion became a stricter pair. Plus two added tests against a real WAL store held open by a second connection.

cmd: pnpm run check-types && pnpm run test:unit

testChange.reason: This task removes the sidecar-copy mechanism outright, so the tests pinning it had to go: the two round-3/round-4 describes asserting copy ORDER and sidecar presence, and the D13 test asserting the db plus sidecars were copied. The D13 test was replaced rather than deleted — same intent (never read the live store in place), now asserting a read-only VACUUM INTO and that copy is never called. Added in their place: a CLI end-to-end read of a WAL-resident row from a live store through the real sqlite3 binary, and two withSqliteSnapshot tests (one snapshot serves many queries; a failed snapshot is query-error). Net coverage of the invariant is higher, not lower.
